# Frequently Asked Questions
Expert answers covering gold rates, karat purities, VAT regulations, making charges, and investment insights across the UAE.
# Q 1 . How often are gold rates updated in the UAE?
Gold rates are compiled from third-party market data and refreshed throughout the trading day when our market feed is available. Every rate table carries a visible Gulf Standard Time timestamp so you know exactly how fresh the numbers are.
# Q 2 . What is the difference between 24K, 22K, 21K, and 18K gold?
24K is pure gold (99.9% purity), making it soft and ideal for bullion bars and coins. 22K contains 91.6% gold, popular for traditional high-carat jewelry. 21K (87.5% purity) and 18K (75.0% purity) contain higher alloy metals for enhanced durability, making them perfect for intricate diamond or gemstone jewelry settings.
# Q 3 . Are making charges included in the spot gold rates shown?
No. The prices displayed on our website reflect the intrinsic melt-value of raw gold per gram in UAE Dirhams (AED). Making charges (Majrool), design complexity fees, and brand premiums are charged separately by retail jewelers in the Dubai Gold Souk.

chunks.title: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.text:
# Q 4 . Is there any VAT or tax on buying gold in the UAE?
Investment-grade gold (purity of 99% or higher in the form of bars, coins, or investment precious metals) is subject to 0% or zero-rated VAT under UAE tax laws. However, retail jewelry purchases are subject to the standard 5% VAT applied on the making charges portion.
# Q 5 . Why do gold prices vary slightly between different shops in Dubai Gold Souk?
While the baseline metal rate is anchored to the global exchange, individual jewelry shops set different making charges depending on the brand reputation, craftsmanship origin (e.g., Italian, local, or Indian design), and whether the item is machine-made or hand-crafted.
# Q 6 . Can international tourists claim VAT refunds on gold purchases in the UAE?
Under the UAE Tax Free shopping system, tourists can claim VAT refunds on eligible retail purchases (including jewelry making charges) upon departure through approved digital schemes like Planet Tax Free at UAE airports, provided they meet minimum spend and validation criteria.
# Q 7 . Is it better to buy gold bars (bullion) or jewelry for investment?

chunks.title: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.text:
For pure investment purposes, 24K gold bars and certified coins are always recommended because they carry minimal fabrication/making premiums and can be liquidated easily at international spot value with negligible buy-back loss.
# Q 8 . How is the gold price per gram calculated from ounce prices?
Global gold is traded in troy ounces (1 troy ounce = 31.1035 grams). To find the 24K gram price in AED, we take the international ounce rate in AED and divide it precisely by 31.1035.
# Q 9 . What factors drive gold price movements in the UAE market?
Key drivers include US Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, US Dollar index strength, geopolitical tensions, global inflation rates, central bank gold reserves purchasing, and localized festive/wedding season demand spikes across Dubai.
# Q 10 . Can I sell gold back to any jeweler in Dubai even if I didn't buy it there?
Yes, the Dubai gold market is highly liquid. Most certified bullion dealers and jewelers will buy back gold items. However, carrying your original purchase invoice and ensuring the hallmark stamp is intact makes the buy-back process faster and smoother.

# Dubai Gold Souk Bargaining Guide 2026: Weights & Charges
You can overpay by hundreds of dirhams at the Dubai Gold Souk without ever being cheated on the gold rate — the money leaks out through two billing practices most first-time buyers never see coming: gross-weight billing and inflated making charges. The souk's 300+ shops along Deira's creek-side streets offer transparent prices and high purity standards, and bargaining is not just accepted, it is expected. This guide shows you exactly how both tricks work and how to beat them in 2026.
# Gross Weight vs Net Weight: The Trick That Costs Buyers Most
Here is the single most important concept in this guide.
When you pick up a necklace with diamonds, enamel, or colored stones, the shop's scale shows the gross weight — the gold plus the stones, enamel, settings, and sometimes even the lac (wax) backing inside Kundan pieces. Stones are worth a fraction of gold's price, yet some shops bill the entire gross weight at the gold rate.
Net weight is the gold alone — and that is the only weight you should pay the gold rate on.
# How different embellishments are treated

chunks.title: Dubai Gold Souk Bargaining Guide 2026: Weights & Charges
chunks.text:
Not all stones are priced the same way, and knowing the difference protects your wallet:
Cubic zirconia and synthetic stones: these cost almost nothing. Their entire weight should be deducted from the billable gold weight, with only a small setting charge (typically AED 20–80 per piece) added to making charges.
Certified natural diamonds: never priced at gold rates. The gold is weighed separately at net weight, and diamonds are priced individually by the 4Cs (carat, cut, clarity, color) with certificates from GIA, IGI, or HRD.
Kundan and Polki jewellery: traditional Kundan sets contain lac (wax/resin) linings behind uncut diamonds, and lac can account for 20–40% of the gross weight. Always demand a written net-gold-weight certificate before buying.
# What to say at the counter
Ask this exact question before any price discussion: "What is the net gold weight, excluding stones and enamel?" If the seller hesitates or refuses to separate it, walk away. Reputable shops will weigh the piece, deduct the embellishments, and write the net weight on your invoice.
# Making Charges: Where the Real Bargaining Happens

chunks.title: Dubai Gold Souk Bargaining Guide 2026: Weights & Charges
chunks.text:
The gold rate is fixed daily and non-negotiable. Making charges — the fee for craftsmanship — are where your bargaining power lives.
# Typical making-charge ranges in the Souk (2026)
Plain 24K coins and simple bars: AED 5–15/gram
Simple chains, plain bangles: AED 10–25/gram
Standard necklaces and rings: AED 20–40/gram
Intricate bridal sets, filigree: AED 40–80+/gram
Designer and branded pieces: AED 60–150+/gram
Mall boutiques, by comparison, often charge AED 40–120+ per gram with little room to negotiate — one reason experienced buyers prefer the Souk. For the full breakdown of how charges and VAT combine, see our guide to gold making charges and VAT in the UAE .
# How to bargain: a step-by-step approach
Know the day's rate first. Check the live rate before you enter — use our gold price calculator to see what the piece should cost before charges.
Compare at least three shops. Making charges for similar designs can differ by AED 200–1,500 on the same piece. Smaller shops often flex more than big branded outlets.
Start at 40% below the quoted making charge. Sellers inflate the opening quote expecting exactly this. A calm counteroffer is part of the ritual, not an insult.

chunks.title: Dubai Gold Souk Bargaining Guide 2026: Weights & Charges
chunks.text:
Bundle purchases. Buying two or three pieces together gives you leverage for a collective discount on charges.
Offer cash. Card payments can attract a 1–2.5% convenience fee at some shops; cash removes the fee and sometimes earns a better price.
Be ready to walk away. The most powerful sentence in the Souk is silence followed by your feet. Sellers frequently call you back with a better price.
Realistic outcome: most buyers can negotiate 15–20% off quoted making charges, and skilled bargainers on plain pieces get up to 30–50% off. A few Arabic phrases — "ghali jiddan" (too expensive) — signal that you know the game.
# VAT and Tourist Refunds: The 5% You Should Not Ignore
Since January 2018, the UAE applies 5% VAT on gold jewellery — calculated on the gold value plus making charges. On a Dh10,000 purchase, that is Dh500. It matters.
Jewellery: 5% VAT applies to the full subtotal (gold + making charges).
Investment-grade gold (24K bars and coins): may qualify for the reverse charge mechanism, effectively zero VAT for the buyer in qualifying transactions. Ask your dealer specifically and make sure the invoice reflects it.

chunks.title: Dubai Gold Souk Bargaining Guide 2026: Weights & Charges
chunks.text:
Tourists: the UAE operates a Tourist VAT Refund scheme. Visitors can claim back VAT paid on purchases (including gold jewellery) when leaving the country, subject to minimum purchase thresholds and the refund process at the airport. Keep your invoices — they are your refund paperwork.
# The Souk vs Meena Bazaar vs Malls: Where Should You Buy?
Making charges AED 12–35/g (the lowest of the three); bargaining is high — up to 30–50% off charges. Best for bullion, 24K bars, and heavy bridal pieces, with an unbeatable bullion selection.
# Meena Bazaar (Bur Dubai)
Making charges AED 18–45/g; bargaining moderate to high. The cultural home of Indian 22K bridal, Kundan, and temple designs; bullion selection is limited.
Making charges AED 40–120+/g; pricing fixed with minimal bargaining. Best for 18K Italian pieces, diamonds, and luxury brands; bullion is rare and carries high premiums.
The Souk wins for investment gold and maximum bargaining. Meena Bazaar — a one-dirham abra ride across the creek — is the cultural home of South Asian bridal designs. Malls win on comfort and luxury brands, at a price.

# Frequently Asked Questions
# Can you bargain in the Dubai Gold Souk?
Yes — bargaining is expected, especially on making charges. The gold rate itself is fixed, but making charges are negotiable, with 15–30% reductions common for confident buyers who compare shops.
# What is the difference between gross weight and net weight?
Gross weight is the total weight of the piece including stones, enamel, and settings. Net weight is the gold alone. You should only pay the gold rate on the net weight; stones and embellishments are priced separately.
# How much are making charges in the Dubai Gold Souk?

chunks.text:
Typically AED 10–50 per gram depending on design complexity — plain pieces at the low end, intricate bridal sets at the high end. These are starting quotes; negotiate before accepting.
# Do tourists pay VAT on gold in Dubai?
Yes, 5% VAT applies on gold jewellery purchases, but tourists can claim refunds under the UAE's Tourist VAT Refund scheme when departing, provided they keep their invoices.
# Is gold cheaper in the Souk or in malls?
The gold rate is the same everywhere; the Souk wins on making charges (often half of mall rates) and bargaining flexibility. Malls charge AED 40–120+/gram in making charges with fixed pricing.
# Should I pay cash or card at the Gold Souk?
Cash is preferred — some shops add 1–2.5% card surcharges, and cash payments can unlock slightly better negotiated prices.
# How do I know the gold is genuine?
Buy only hallmarked pieces (look for 916/875/750 stamps), insist on an itemized invoice showing karat, net weight, rate, and charges, and stick to established shops. For bars, buy sealed with assay certificates.

# Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE: Full Cost Guide
When you buy gold jewellery in the UAE, you pay for three things: the gold itself, the making charges, and 5% VAT. The last two can add 10–25% to your bill, and both are widely misunderstood. This guide explains exactly how making charges and VAT are calculated, what is negotiable, and how to keep the extra costs as low as possible.
# Making Charges Explained
# What are making charges?
Making charges (also called workmanship or labour charges) are the jeweller's fee for turning raw gold into a finished piece — designing, casting, setting, polishing, and finishing. They pay for craftsmanship, not metal.
# How making charges are calculated
In the UAE, making charges are almost always quoted per gram of the finished piece. The full price works like this:
Total price = (weight × day's gold rate) + (weight × making charge per gram) + 5% VAT on the sum
Example — a 20-gram 22K necklace at AED 451/gram with AED 35/gram making charges:
Gold value: 20 × 451 = AED 9,020
Making charges: 20 × 35 = AED 700

chunks.title: Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE: Full Cost Guide
chunks.text:
Notice that the making charges added AED 700 plus another AED 35 in VAT — nearly 7.5% on top of the gold value. You can run your own numbers before you shop with our jewellery cost calculator , which breaks down gold value, making charges, and VAT for any piece.
# Typical making-charge ranges in the UAE
Plain gold coins, simple bars: AED 5–15 per gram
Simple chains, plain bangles: AED 10–25 per gram
Standard necklaces, rings: AED 20–40 per gram
Intricate bridal sets, filigree: AED 40–80+ per gram
Designer and branded pieces: AED 60–150+ per gram (often charged as a percentage of value)
These are starting quotes, not final prices. Everything except the gold rate itself is negotiable.
# What drives making charges up?
Intricacy: hand-finished filigree and detailed engraving cost more than cast pieces
Brand premium: international brands charge for the name as well as the craft
Low weight, high detail: a delicate 5-gram ring can carry higher per-gram charges than a 50-gram bangle
Stones and settings: diamond and gemstone setting is priced separately, and steeply
# Making charges are NOT refunded on resale

chunks.title: Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE: Full Cost Guide
chunks.text:
This is the point most buyers miss: when you sell gold jewellery, the buyer pays only for the gold content — weight × karat rate, minus a small margin. Making charges vanish the moment you walk out of the shop. The AED 700 making charge in the example above is money you will never recover.
So for investment, buy 24K coins and bars with minimal making charges. For jewellery you love and will wear, accept making charges as the price of beauty — but negotiate them hard. Our guide to selling gold in the UAE explains exactly how buyback pricing works.
# VAT on Gold in the UAE (5%)
Since January 2018, the UAE has charged 5% VAT on gold jewellery. It applies to the gold value plus the making charges — the full subtotal — on most retail gold jewellery purchases.
# What about gold bars and coins?
Investment-grade gold (typically 24K bars meeting certain purity criteria) can qualify for the reverse charge mechanism , which means VAT is accounted for differently — often effectively zero for the buyer in qualifying transactions. Ask your dealer specifically; the rules depend on the product type and whether you are a business or an individual.

chunks.title: Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE: Full Cost Guide
chunks.text:
Visitors to the UAE can reclaim VAT on eligible purchases through the Tourist Refund Scheme :
Shop at retailers displaying "Tax Free" / Planet Tax Free signage
Ask for a tax-free invoice at the time of purchase
Validate and claim at the airport before departure (kiosks and counters; refunds go to card or cash)
The refund applies to the VAT on your gold purchase too — on a AED 10,000 jewellery bill, that is AED 500 back. Always ask the shop whether they participate before you pay.
A legitimate invoice must show VAT separately (5% of the subtotal). If a shop offers a "discount for no VAT invoice," refuse. That is tax evasion, and you lose your proof of purchase, your tourist refund eligibility, and any buyback rights.
# How to Minimise Your Total Cost: 9 Strategies
Negotiate making charges first. This is the biggest variable. Aim for 20–40% off the opening quote at the souk.
Compare per gram, not per piece. Two shops' "AED 800 making" quotes mean nothing until divided by weight.
Choose simpler designs if budget matters — a plain 22K bangle can carry one-third the making charges of an engraved one.

chunks.title: Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE: Full Cost Guide
chunks.text:
Buy during promotions. Dubai Shopping Festival and jeweller anniversary sales often feature reduced or zero making charges.
Ask about wastage charges. Some shops add "wastage" (metal lost in crafting) on top of making charges. Question it — on modern machine-made pieces it is often negligible or already included.
Consider 24K coins for gifts and investment — minimal making charges, maximum resale value.
Tourists: use the VAT refund. It is a straight 5% saving for ten minutes at the airport.
Pay attention to stone weight. Make sure diamonds and gemstones are weighed and priced separately, not charged at the gold rate.
Get everything in writing. Weight, karat, gold rate, making charge per gram, VAT — all on the stamped invoice.
# Making Charges on Diamond and Gemstone Jewellery

chunks.title: Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE: Full Cost Guide
chunks.text:
When a piece contains diamonds or coloured stones, the pricing structure changes. Stones are priced separately — per carat for diamonds, per piece or per carat for coloured gems — and the setting labour is added on top of the gold making charge. Always ask for three separate lines on the invoice: gold value, stone value, and total making/setting charges. A common trick is to inflate the stone value while quoting a "low" making charge, so compare the all-in price per piece across shops rather than any single line item. For diamond jewellery, insist on a grading certificate from a recognised lab; without one, you cannot verify what you are paying for.
# Worked Example: Spotting a Bad Deal
Two shops quote on the same 15-gram 22K bracelet (gold at AED 451/gram = AED 6,765 gold value):
Shop A: making AED 45/gram → AED 675 + VAT → total AED 7,812
Shop B: making AED 25/gram → AED 375 + VAT → total AED 7,497
Same gold, same weight — an AED 315 difference purely from making charges. This is why the per-gram question matters more than any other. Before any purchase, check the live Dubai gold rate so you know the true gold value you are measuring against.
# Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.title: Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE: Full Cost Guide
chunks.text:
# Are making charges negotiable in Dubai?
Yes — especially at the Gold Souk. Mall brand stores negotiate less, but asking during promotions can still work.
# What is a reasonable making charge per gram in the UAE?
AED 10–25/gram for simple pieces, AED 20–40 for standard jewellery, AED 40+/gram for intricate or branded work — all before negotiation.
# Do I pay VAT on gold coins in Dubai?
Investment-grade 24K bars and coins may qualify for special VAT treatment under the reverse charge mechanism. Standard jewellery coins attract 5% VAT. Confirm with the dealer.
# Can tourists really get the VAT back on gold?
Yes, through the Tourist Refund Scheme at the airport, provided you bought from a participating retailer and kept the tax invoice.
# Are making charges included in the resale price?
No. Resale pays for gold content only. Making charges are never recovered — buy investment gold as low-making-charge coins and bars.
# What are "wastage charges"?
A traditional fee for gold supposedly lost during crafting. On modern pieces it is often minimal; always ask whether it is included in the making charge or added separately, and challenge it.

# Dubai Gold Souk Shopping Guide: Bargain & Buy Safely
The Dubai Gold Souk in Deira is one of the best places in the world to buy gold — hundreds of shops, transparent daily rates, and making charges you can negotiate down by 20–40%. It rewards preparation, though. Walk in knowing the day's rate and how bargaining works, and you will leave with beautiful gold at a fair price. Walk in blind, and you may overpay.
This guide covers how the souk works, how to bargain step by step, how to spot a trustworthy shop, and the red flags that should make you walk away.
# How the Gold Souk Works
The souk is a traditional covered market near Dubai Creek in Deira. Unlike a mall, each shop is independently owned, prices are negotiable, and the atmosphere is lively and old-school. A few things to know before you go:
Opening hours: most shops open around 9:30–10:00 AM and close around 9:30–10:00 PM. Many close for a midday break (roughly 1:00–4:00 PM), though timings vary.
Getting there: Al Ras metro station (Green Line) is a short walk away, or take an abra (water taxi) across the creek from Bur Dubai for AED 1 — a classic Dubai experience.

chunks.title: Dubai Gold Souk Shopping Guide: Bargain & Buy Safely
chunks.text:
Best time to visit: weekday mornings are calmest. Evenings are atmospheric but crowded.
# Before You Go: Do Your Homework
Check the day's gold rate. The Dubai Jewellery Group publishes official rates each morning. Check the live Dubai gold rate on your phone before entering any shop — this is your single most important piece of leverage.
Decide your karat and approximate weight. Know whether you want 22K, 21K, or 18K, and have a rough idea of the design and weight range. If you are unsure, read our guide to understanding gold karats first.
Set a budget in dirhams , including making charges and 5% VAT.
Bring your phone calculator. You will use it constantly — or use our gold price calculator to price a piece before you even arrive.
# Bargaining at the Gold Souk: A Step-by-Step Approach
Negotiation is expected — no shopkeeper is offended by a counter-offer. Here is how experienced buyers do it:
# Step 1: Separate the components
Ask the shopkeeper to break the price into three parts: gold weight × day's rate , making charges , and VAT . The gold price itself is fixed to the market; the making charge is where the negotiation lives.
# Step 2: Question the making charge

chunks.title: Dubai Gold Souk Shopping Guide: Bargain & Buy Safely
chunks.text:
Making charges at the souk typically start at AED 15–60+ per gram depending on intricacy. Ask: "What is your making charge per gram on this piece?" Then ask the same question at two more shops for comparable designs.
# Step 3: Make your counter-offer
A reasonable opening counter is 30–40% below the quoted making charge. The shopkeeper will counter, and you will usually meet somewhere in the middle — often 20–30% below the first quote.
# Step 4: Bundle for leverage
Buying a set (necklace + earrings, or multiple bangles) gives you real leverage. Ask for a bundled making-charge rate.
# Step 5: Be prepared to walk away
The most powerful negotiating tool is your feet. Thank the shopkeeper politely and walk out. In many cases you will hear a better price before you reach the next shop.
"What is today's rate?" — confirms they are using the official price

The Gold Souk is well regulated, but quality varies. Look for:
Longevity and reputation. Shops that have operated for decades (many display their founding year) have reputations to protect.
Clear rate displays. Trustworthy shops show the day's gold rate prominently.
Detailed invoices. A proper invoice lists weight, karat, gold value, making charges, and VAT separately. Never accept a vague handwritten total.
Hallmarked gold. Every piece should carry a karat hallmark stamp.
Willingness to explain. Good shopkeepers happily explain weight, purity, and charges. Evasive answers are a warning sign.
Well-known names with multiple branches across the souk and malls — such as long-established family jewellers — are generally safe bets, but always verify the invoice details yourself.
# Scams and Traps: What to Watch For
Outright fraud is rare because the market is regulated, but these practices can cost you money:
# 1. Inflated making charges for tourists

Quoting the gross weight (including stones or non-gold parts) at the gold rate. Defence: ask for the net gold weight and confirm stones are priced separately.

Price: the souk is usually lower and negotiable; mall prices are higher and mostly fixed

# Is bargaining acceptable at the Dubai Gold Souk?

chunks.title: Dubai Gold Souk Shopping Guide: Bargain & Buy Safely
chunks.text:
Yes — it is expected. The gold rate is fixed, but making charges are negotiable. Polite, informed bargaining typically saves 20–40% on making charges.

Dubai's gold market is strictly regulated. Buy from established shops, check the hallmark stamp, confirm karat and weight on a detailed invoice, and you are protected.

Most shops open 9:30–10:00 AM to 9:30–10:00 PM, with many closing for a midday break. Friday afternoons can be quieter.
# Can I get a VAT refund as a tourist?
Yes. Keep your invoices from shops participating in the Tourist Refund Scheme and claim at the airport.
# Is it safe to carry large amounts of cash at the souk?
The area is generally safe and well-policed, but card payments are widely accepted — there is rarely a need to carry large cash sums. Some shops offer small cash discounts.
# Should I buy from the first shop I like?
No. Note the design and price, visit 2–3 more shops, then return to the best offer. Comparison is your strongest tool.

# How to Buy Gold in Dubai: The Complete 2026 Guide
Dubai is one of the best places in the world to buy gold: prices follow a transparent daily rate, the selection is enormous, and making charges are negotiable. To buy well, you need to know four things — where to shop, which karat to choose, how the price is built, and how to negotiate. This guide walks you through all of it before you spend a single dirham.
# Why Dubai Is One of the Best Places in the World to Buy Gold
Gold has been traded in Dubai for over a century, and the emirate remains one of the largest physical gold trading hubs on the planet. Several factors make buying gold in Dubai attractive:
Transparent daily pricing. The Dubai Jewellery Group publishes official retail gold rates every morning, and most reputable shops display them clearly. You always know the base price before negotiation begins.
No import duty on gold for travellers. Tourists can carry gold jewellery for personal use back home (subject to their home country's customs rules), which makes Dubai a popular destination for wedding gold shopping.

chunks.title: How to Buy Gold in Dubai: The Complete 2026 Guide
chunks.text:
Huge selection. From the historic Gold Souk in Deira to gleaming mall boutiques, you can find everything from simple 24K coins to intricate 22K bridal sets.
Regulated market. Gold sold in the UAE must be hallmarked, and shops operate under strict consumer-protection rules.
As of October 2026, with international gold prices near historic highs (around $4,170 per troy ounce), understanding exactly what you are paying for matters more than ever. Start by checking the live Dubai gold rate — every price in this guide is built on it.
# Where to Buy Gold in Dubai
# 1. Dubai Gold Souk, Deira
The Gold Souk is the beating heart of Dubai's gold trade — a covered market with hundreds of shops selling gold, diamonds, and precious stones. It is the best place for:
The widest selection and most competitive making charges
Traditional designs (Indian, Arabic, and Pakistani styles especially)
Serious bargaining — negotiation is expected here

chunks.title: How to Buy Gold in Dubai: The Complete 2026 Guide
chunks.text:
The souk is easily reached by metro (Al Ras station on the Green Line) or abra across Dubai Creek. Go in the morning for a calmer experience, or in the evening when the market is at its liveliest. Our Gold Souk shopping guide covers bargaining tactics and scam warnings in detail.
# 2. Mall Jewellery Stores
Malls like Dubai Mall, Mall of the Emirates, and Deira City Centre host international and regional jewellery brands (Malabar Gold & Diamonds, Joyalukkas, Kalyan Jewellers, Tanishq, Damas, and others). Expect:
Fixed, clearly displayed prices with less room for negotiation
Strong after-sales service, warranties, and buyback policies
Modern, lightweight designs
# 3. Online Gold Retailers
Several UAE jewellers now sell online with home delivery. This can be convenient for standard items like coins and simple bangles, but for high-value pieces most buyers still prefer to see and feel the gold in person.
# Understanding Gold Karats: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
The karat tells you the purity of the gold. In Dubai you will mainly encounter four:
24K (99.9% pure). The purest form. Best for coins, bars, and investment. Too soft for most jewellery.

chunks.title: How to Buy Gold in Dubai: The Complete 2026 Guide
chunks.text:
22K (91.6% pure). The classic choice for jewellery in the UAE, especially among South Asian buyers. Strong enough for daily wear while retaining high gold content.
21K (87.5% pure). Very popular in the Arab world for its rich colour and durability. Common in Gulf-style designs.
18K (75% pure). Preferred for diamond-studded and designer pieces where strength matters more than purity. Common in European-style jewellery.
Your choice depends on purpose: investment → 24K coins/bars; jewellery → 22K or 21K; diamond or designer pieces → 18K. Use our karat converter to compare prices across purities, and see our full guide: Understanding Gold Karats .
# How Gold Prices Work in Dubai
Gold in Dubai is priced per gram, and the price has three components:
The international gold price , converted to dirhams per gram for the relevant karat. This is the non-negotiable base.
Making charges — the jeweller's fee for crafting the piece. This is where negotiation happens.
5% VAT — applied to the total (gold value + making charges).

These move daily with the international market. Always check the current rate before you shop, and confirm the shop is using the day's official rate. Our gold price calculator works out the full cost of any piece — gold value, making charges, and VAT included.
# Making Charges and VAT: What You Must Know
Making charges typically range from AED 10 to AED 60+ per gram depending on design complexity. Simple bangles and chains carry low charges; intricate bridal sets carry high ones. Making charges are almost always negotiable — treat the first quote as a starting point.
VAT at 5% applies to gold jewellery purchases in the UAE. Key points:
VAT applies to the full amount: gold value + making charges.
24K gold bars and coins of investment grade may qualify for special treatment — ask the dealer.
Tourists can claim a VAT refund on eligible purchases through the Tourist Refund Scheme (look for "Tax Free" signage and keep your receipts).
See our full guide: Gold Making Charges & VAT in the UAE .
# How to Negotiate the Best Price
Bargaining is part of the culture, especially at the Gold Souk. Practical tips:
Know the day's rate before you walk in. Check the live price on your phone.

chunks.title: How to Buy Gold in Dubai: The Complete 2026 Guide
chunks.text:
Separate the gold price from the making charges. Agree the weight and karat price first, then negotiate making charges.
Ask for the making charge per gram, not a lump sum. This makes comparison easy.
Get quotes from 3–4 shops for the same design before committing.
Paying cash can earn a small discount at some souk shops (though card payments are standard and safe).
Walk away politely if the price feels wrong. Good shops will often call you back with a better offer.
A realistic target: negotiate making charges down 20–40% from the opening quote on standard designs.
# The Best Times to Buy Gold in Dubai
During gold price dips. Watch the international price; even a $30–50/oz drop translates into meaningful savings per gram.
Dubai Shopping Festival (typically December–January). Many jewellers run promotions with reduced or zero making charges.
Weekday mornings. Shops are quieter and staff have more time (and incentive) to negotiate.
Avoid buying in a rush before weddings or festivals if you can — demand peaks push making charges up.
# Checklist: Before You Pay
Verified the day's official gold rate
Confirmed karat and exact weight on the receipt

chunks.title: How to Buy Gold in Dubai: The Complete 2026 Guide
chunks.text:
Negotiated making charges (per gram, in writing)
Checked the hallmark stamp on the piece
Confirmed VAT amount separately on the invoice
Asked about the shop's buyback/exchange policy
Kept the invoice — you will need it if you ever sell
# Frequently Asked Questions
# Is gold cheaper in Dubai than in India or Pakistan?
Often yes for the same karat, because Dubai has no import duty on gold and a highly competitive retail market. However, factor in making charges, VAT (partially refundable for tourists), and your home country's customs duty on arrival.
# Can tourists buy gold in Dubai?
Absolutely. There are no restrictions on tourists buying gold. Keep your invoices, and check your home country's duty-free allowance for gold before you fly back.
# What is the VAT on gold in Dubai?
5% VAT applies to gold jewellery (gold value + making charges). Tourists may claim a refund under the Tourist Refund Scheme.
# Is the gold in Dubai's Gold Souk genuine?
Yes — the market is strictly regulated and gold must be hallmarked. Buy from established shops, insist on a detailed invoice, and check the hallmark.
# Should I buy 22K or 24K gold in Dubai?

chunks.title: How to Buy Gold in Dubai: The Complete 2026 Guide
chunks.text:
For jewellery, 22K (or 21K for Gulf styles). For investment, 24K coins or bars. 24K is too soft for everyday jewellery.
# Can I bargain at Dubai mall jewellery stores?
Less than at the souk, but it never hurts to ask — especially on making charges or during promotions. At the Gold Souk, bargaining is expected.

# Selling Gold in the UAE: Prices, Places & Best Tips
Selling gold in the UAE is simple once you know one rule: buyers pay for the gold content of your item, nothing else. Your payout is the net gold weight × karat purity × the day's buyback rate — typically 1–3% below the retail rate, with making charges and VAT never repaid. This guide covers where to sell, the documents you need, and how to make sure you get a fair price.
# How Gold Buyback Pricing Works
The formula every buyer uses is:
Payout = net gold weight × karat purity × day's buyback rate
Three things to understand:
The buyback rate is slightly below the retail selling rate. The difference (the dealer's margin) is typically 1–3% for standard items. This is normal and fair.
Making charges are not paid. That AED 40/gram craftsmanship premium you paid when buying? It is worth zero on resale. Only the metal counts.
Stones are excluded or valued separately. Diamonds and gemstones are removed from the weight calculation (or appraised separately by specialists).
You sell a 22K necklace weighing 25 grams. The day's 22K buyback rate is AED 445/gram (slightly below the AED 451 retail rate):
25 × 445 = AED 11,125 payout

chunks.title: Selling Gold in the UAE: Prices, Places & Best Tips
chunks.text:
If you originally paid AED 12,000 (gold + making + VAT), the ~AED 875 difference is the making charges and VAT you never recover. This is the cost of having worn beautiful jewellery — factor it in before you buy, not after. Before visiting any buyer, estimate your payout with our sell gold estimator so you know what a fair offer looks like.
# Where to Sell Gold in the UAE
# 1. The shop you bought it from
Your first stop. Many jewellers offer buyback guarantees — sometimes at favourable terms for their own pieces, especially if you originally bought from them and kept the invoice. Some offer better rates if you exchange for new jewellery rather than taking cash.
# 2. Gold Souk buyers, Deira
Dozens of shops in and around the Gold Souk buy gold daily. Competition keeps margins thin — get quotes from 3–4 buyers before deciding. This is usually where you will find the best cash price.
# 3. Mall jewellery stores
Major brands buy back their own pieces and sometimes others'. Rates may be slightly lower than the souk, but the process is formal and comfortable.
# 4. Specialised gold-buying companies

chunks.title: Selling Gold in the UAE: Prices, Places & Best Tips
chunks.text:
A growing number of UAE companies specialise in buying gold, with transparent per-gram rates published online. Useful for comparing against souk quotes.
# 5. Banks (for investment bars)
Some UAE banks buy back investment-grade bars they sold, occasionally at very tight spreads. Ask your bank if you hold their minted products.
Avoid: pawn-style shops offering far below market, and any buyer who will not test the gold in front of you or provide a written quote.
Emirates ID (or passport for visitors) — buyers are legally required to record seller identity for higher-value transactions
Original purchase invoice — proves karat, weight, and origin; strengthens your negotiating position and speeds up the process
Any certificates — for diamond-studded pieces, bring grading certificates
Without an invoice, the buyer must assay (test) the gold themselves, which is fine, but you lose the leverage of documented weight and purity.
# The Selling Process: Step by Step
Check the day's rate — start with the live Dubai gold rate so you know the fair buyback range.
Clean your gold gently (warm water, mild soap, soft brush) — presentation will not change the assay, but it helps.

chunks.title: Selling Gold in the UAE: Prices, Places & Best Tips
chunks.text:
Get 3–4 written quotes. State the karat and weight from your invoice; let each buyer verify independently.
Watch the testing. Reputable buyers test purity in front of you — either with an electronic tester or a small acid test on an inconspicuous spot. For large lots, XRF (X-ray fluorescence) testing is non-destructive and precise.
Confirm the math. Weight × purity × rate, minus nothing else. Ask about any deductions before agreeing.
Get paid securely. Bank transfer or manager's cheque for large amounts; cash is common for smaller lots. Get a receipt.
# Exchange vs Cash: Which Is Better?
Many jewellers offer two prices:
Cash buyback: the standard rate described above
Exchange value: a higher effective rate if you put the money toward new jewellery in the same shop (sometimes 2–5% better, plus waived making charges on the new piece)
If you are upgrading rather than exiting, exchange almost always beats cash . Get both quotes in writing and compare. If you do exchange, our guide on how to buy gold in Dubai will help you get the best deal on the new piece.
# Tips for Getting the Best Price

chunks.title: Selling Gold in the UAE: Prices, Places & Best Tips
chunks.text:
Sell when the market is strong. Gold near all-time highs (around $4,170/oz as of October 2026) is the time to take profit — do not sell into a dip unless you must.
Keep invoices forever. They are your proof of weight and karat.
Separate high-karat from low-karat pieces before getting quotes — do not let a buyer average them down.
Remove non-gold parts yourself if possible (watch straps, non-gold clasps) so they are not weighed against you.
Ask for the rate, not just the total. "What is your buyback rate per gram for 22K today?" — then do the math yourself.
Time of day matters little; the day matters a lot. Rates update with the international market, so selling on a strong-price day beats any intraday timing.
Consider partial selling. You do not have to sell everything at once — stagger sales if you expect prices to rise further.
# What About Selling Gold Coins and Bars?
Investment-grade 24K bars and sealed coins are the easiest gold to sell:
They trade at the tightest spreads (often within 1% of the market rate)
Sealed, certified products need no assay — the seal is the proof
Banks, dealers, and souk buyers all compete for them

chunks.title: Selling Gold in the UAE: Prices, Places & Best Tips
chunks.text:
Never open sealed packaging unless the buyer requires it — breaking the seal can trigger an assay discount.
# Red Flags: When to Walk Away
Buyer refuses to test in front of you
Quote is more than ~5% below the day's fair buyback rate with no explanation
Pressure to decide immediately ("this rate expires in five minutes")
No written quote or receipt offered
Buyer wants to keep your invoice "for their records" without giving you a copy
# Frequently Asked Questions
# What documents do I need to sell gold in Dubai?
Emirates ID (or passport), plus your original purchase invoice. Certificates help for diamond pieces.
# How much less than the market price will I get?
Typically 1–3% below the retail selling rate for standard jewellery; under 1% for investment bars. Making charges and VAT are never recovered.
# Can tourists sell gold in the UAE?
Yes. Bring your passport and any purchase invoices. The process is the same as for residents.
# Is it better to exchange old gold for new jewellery?
Usually yes — exchange rates are 2–5% better than cash buyback, and shops often reduce making charges on the new piece.
# Do I pay VAT when selling gold?

chunks.title: Selling Gold in the UAE: Prices, Places & Best Tips
chunks.text:
No — VAT was already paid when you bought it. Private sellers do not charge VAT on the sale.
# Should I sell now while gold is near record highs?
If your goal is profit-taking, strong markets are the logical time. But nobody can predict the top — many sellers stagger sales across several weeks to average their exit price.

# Gold Karats Explained: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
A karat measures how pure your gold is, out of 24 parts. 24K is 99.9% pure gold, 22K is 91.6%, 21K is 87.5%, and 18K is 75% — and that difference changes the price per gram, the colour, and how well a piece survives daily wear. This guide explains how the four karats compare in the UAE, what each costs, and which one fits your purpose.
# What Does "Karat" Actually Mean?
A karat measures gold purity in 24 parts. 24K means 24 out of 24 parts are pure gold (99.9%). 18K means 18 out of 24 parts are gold (75%), with the remaining 6 parts made up of alloy metals like copper, silver, zinc, or nickel.
The alloys are not filler — they change the metal's properties:
More alloy = harder, more durable metal , but less gold content
Less alloy = softer, richer yellow colour , but the piece bends and scratches more easily
Copper-heavy alloys give rose gold its pink tone; nickel/palladium alloys create white gold
To compare the cost of the same piece in different purities, use our karat converter — it converts any price or weight between 24K, 22K, 21K, and 18K instantly.
# The Four Karats You Will Meet in the UAE
# 24K Gold — 99.9% Pure

chunks.title: Gold Karats Explained: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
chunks.text:
The purest commercially available gold. In the UAE, 24K is used almost exclusively for investment bars and coins, and some traditional bridal pieces (rarely worn daily).
Pros: maximum gold value; easiest to resell at close to market price; favourable VAT treatment for investment-grade bars. Cons: very soft — jewellery in 24K bends, dents, and loses shape with daily wear.
Indicative UAE price (Oct 2026): ~AED 492/gram.
# 22K Gold — 91.6% Pure
The workhorse of UAE jewellery, especially among South Asian buyers. The 8.4% alloy content gives it enough strength for bangles, necklaces, and rings worn daily, while keeping gold content high.
Pros: excellent balance of purity and durability; strong resale value; the standard for bridal gold in Indian and Pakistani communities. Cons: slightly less rich in colour than 24K; still softer than 21K/18K.
Indicative UAE price (Oct 2026): ~AED 451/gram.
# 21K Gold — 87.5% Pure
The favourite across the Arab world. That extra alloy versus 22K makes 21K noticeably harder — ideal for the bold, high-relief Gulf designs (heavy necklaces, wide bangles, intricate filigree) that would deform in softer gold.

chunks.title: Gold Karats Explained: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
chunks.text:
Pros: durable for statement pieces; beautiful deep yellow colour; strong cultural preference in the GCC keeps resale liquid. Cons: lower gold content than 22K; slightly lower per-gram value.
Indicative UAE price (Oct 2026): ~AED 431/gram.
The international standard for fine jewellery. In the UAE, 18K dominates diamond-studded pieces (diamonds need strong settings), designer and European-style jewellery, and watches and luxury items.
Pros: hardest and most durable of the four; holds gemstones securely; widest range of colours (yellow, white, rose). Cons: lowest gold content — you are paying significantly for craftsmanship and brand.
Indicative UAE price (Oct 2026): ~AED 369/gram.
# Karat Comparison at a Glance
24K — 99.9% pure: best for investment (bars, coins); very soft; ~AED 492/gram*
22K — 91.6% pure: best for jewellery and bridal sets; good durability; ~AED 451/gram*
21K — 87.5% pure: best for Gulf-style statement pieces; very good durability; ~AED 431/gram*
18K — 75% pure: best for diamond and designer pieces; excellent durability; ~AED 369/gram*
*Based on a ~$4,170/oz international price, October 2026. Check the live Dubai gold rate for today's per-gram prices in every karat.

chunks.title: Gold Karats Explained: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
chunks.text:
# Which Karat Should UAE Buyers Choose?
24K, without question. Buy minted bars or coins from reputable dealers, keep the sealed packaging and invoice, and you will be able to sell at very close to the market price anywhere in the world. Avoid "investment jewellery" — making charges and design premiums evaporate on resale.
# For bridal and occasion jewellery
22K if you follow South Asian traditions; 21K if you prefer Gulf styles. Both hold value well and suit the heavy designs bridal wear demands.
22K for plain gold pieces; 18K for anything with diamonds or gemstones. 24K is simply too soft for rings and bangles you wear every day.
22K coins are the classic UAE gift for weddings, births, and festivals — recognisable, liquid, and culturally appropriate.
# How Karat Affects Price (With an Example)
Take a 10-gram necklace. Using indicative October 2026 rates:
24K: 10g × AED 492 = AED 4,920 (gold value)
22K: 10g × AED 451 = AED 4,510
21K: 10g × AED 431 = AED 4,310
18K: 10g × AED 369 = AED 3,690

chunks.title: Gold Karats Explained: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
chunks.text:
The difference between 24K and 18K on the same weight is over AED 1,200 — before making charges and VAT. This is why confirming the karat on the invoice matters so much. Our guide on how to buy gold in Dubai shows how karat, making charges, and VAT combine in a real purchase.
# Hallmarks: How to Verify Karat
Every gold item sold in the UAE must be hallmarked. Look for:
24K: stamped "999" or "24K"
22K: stamped "916" or "22K"
21K: stamped "875" or "21K"
18K: stamped "750" or "18K"
The number is the parts-per-thousand purity (916 = 91.6%). If a piece has no hallmark, do not buy it — regardless of what the seller claims.
# Gold Colour and Karat: Why 22K Looks Different From 18K

chunks.title: Gold Karats Explained: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
chunks.text:
Pure gold has a rich, warm yellow colour. As alloy content rises, the colour shifts: copper-heavy alloys push the tone toward rose or pink, while silver-heavy alloys lighten it toward a paler yellow. This is why 22K jewellery has that deep, unmistakable "gold" look buyers associate with value, while 18K pieces — especially white or rose gold — look deliberately different. In the UAE market, the deep yellow of 21K and 22K is culturally prized, which is one reason those karats dominate bridal and occasion jewellery. If you love the classic gold colour, stay at 21K or above; if you prefer modern white or rose tones, 18K is where those live.
# Common Karat Mistakes to Avoid
Buying 24K jewellery for daily wear. It will deform. Buy 24K for investment, not for your wrist.
Assuming higher karat always means better value. An 18K designer piece can cost more than a 22K bangle — you are paying for design, not just gold.
Ignoring the karat on the invoice. Verbal promises mean nothing; the karat must be written on your receipt.
Mixing karats in a set without realising. Check every piece in a bridal set individually.
# Frequently Asked Questions
# Which gold karat is most popular in Dubai?

chunks.title: Gold Karats Explained: 24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 18K
chunks.text:

# Understanding gold karats
Karat measures gold purity out of 24 parts: 24K means 24 parts pure gold (99.9%), 22K means 22 parts gold and 2 parts alloy (91.6%), down to 10K at just 41.7% gold. Lower karats are harder, more durable, and cheaper per gram.
Genuine pieces carry a hallmark showing fineness in parts per thousand: 999 for 24K, 916 for 22K, 875 for 21K, 750 for 18K, 585 for 14K and 417 for 10K. This stamp is your most reliable reference when buying at the Gold Souk or selling to a jeweller — counterfeit pieces can carry fake stamps, so always buy from reputable shops.
In the UAE and Gulf, 22K and 21K dominate everyday jewellery, while 18K is preferred for diamond settings because the harder alloy grips stones securely. Investment bars and coins are usually 24K (999.9) to track the global spot price as closely as possible.

Karat measures gold purity out of 24 parts: 24K is 99.9% pure gold, 22K is 91.6%, 21K is 87.5%, 18K is 75%, 14K is 58.5% and 10K is 41.7%. The rest is alloy metals that add strength.
# Q 2 . What do hallmark numbers like 916 or 750 mean?
They are the fineness in parts per thousand: 916 means 91.6% gold (22K), 875 means 87.5% (21K), and 750 means 75% (18K). Always check the hallmark before buying or selling.
# Q 3 . Which karat is best for jewellery in the UAE?
22K and 21K dominate UAE jewellery for their rich colour and good value; 18K is preferred for diamond settings because the harder alloy holds stones better. 24K is too soft for most jewellery and is used for bars and coins.

Yes — 14K gold contains 58.5% pure gold mixed with alloys. It is durable and affordable, common in Western markets, though less popular than 18K–22K in the UAE and Gulf.

# How buyback pricing works
When you sell used gold, the dealer pays only for the gold content at below the market rate, because they carry melting, refining and resale costs plus their margin. In Dubai’s Gold Souk the discount typically runs 3–8% off the melt value — adjust the percentage in the calculator to match the offer you hear in the shop.
Remember that the making charges you paid when buying are never recovered on resale, which is why jewellery is a weaker investment than bars. Before selling, compare at least two or three shops and never accept the first offer you hear.
